issues: Non-blocking, cover tag: 'ASIA AI · POLICY' on an Australian story. DESIGN.md's REGION list has no OCEANIA/AUSTRALIA/APAC, and GLOBAL is only for multi-country stories, so ASIA is the closest allowed value. Strictly, Australia is not in Asia, so the tag is a little misleading. The headline names AUSTRALIA, so no reader will mistake where the story is. Recommend a DESIGN.md decision (add OCEANIA or APAC, or a rule mapping Australia/NZ to ASIA) before the next Australian or NZ story.

Non-blocking, cover image: AI-generated (Higgsfield URL), shows no people or children, no readable text and no visible logos or brands. The empty child's bedroom at night with a crib, toys and a glowing speech bubble behind frosted glass is moody but not inappropriate. Behind the glass, under the bubble, there is a faint vertical shadow that a viewer could read as a ghostly figure. It is not a recognizable person, but if the image is regenerated, ask for an even, shadow-free glass panel.

Non-blocking, wording close to the source: slide 4 ('The wording covers a child's dependence on a chatbot. It does not cover adults who use AI companions.' and 'The rule follows concerns abroad about AI companions and children.') and slide 6 ('The framework would set new online safety standards for social media, games, apps and chatbots') match the quoted TNW text in facts[] almost word for word, without quote marks. The source is credited and TNW is not a reference account, so this does not fail the post. Still, CLAUDE.md asks for newly written English sentences, so suggest rewording these lines.

Non-blocking, credit: the caption and threads_caption both credit The Next Web with the article title, and slide 8 has the source block. TNW's article credits Josh Butler's reporting for The Guardian, so an optional 'via The Guardian' would credit the reporting more fully.

Checked, OK: tone is neutral. Nothing mocks Australia, Albanese, Chaney, the parties or Australians. 'KIDS' AI BFFS' is informal but echoes the PM's 'best friend' quote and does not make light of children. The hook says 'takes on', and slides 2 to 7 support it, including 'It is not law yet'. Not clickbait.
Checked, OK: there are no affiliate, referral or tracking links and no sponsored 'tools we use' mention in the slides, caption or threads_caption. 'Weekly digest: link in bio' is not an ad.

Checked, OK: the rendered slides 01 to 08 use only the DESIGN.md colors (ink, paper, muted, a single yellow accent, line) and fonts (Anton for the cover title, Inter Tight elsewhere). At most 2 accent highlights per body slide. No real-person images anywhere. Nothing in the layout or wording looks copied from a reference account.
